The fault, as main holds it: `deploy/values-production.yaml` names the metrics port `http-metrics` (`metrics.portName: http-metrics`), but `deploy/scrape.yaml`, the ServiceMonitor, still picks its endpoint with `port: metrics`. The comment in scrape.yaml says the ServiceMonitor finds the endpoint by the port's name, and that a name matching no port gives "a target list with nothing in it" rather than an error. So with these two files as they are, Prometheus has nothing to scrape. That fits the metrics stopping while the shop kept serving.

About the deployed revision: c3c36da3c66c07707f227b7e70b26813083061f3 is not in main's history, and I haven't read it. The investigation describes its change as `ports.metrics.portName`, which is a different key path from main's `metrics.portName`. All I can say about c3c36da is what the investigation reports: it renamed the metrics port to `http-metrics` and the scrape still asks for `metrics`. Everything else here describes main.

The fix: in `deploy/scrape.yaml`, change the endpoint's `port: metrics` to `port: http-metrics` so it matches the name in values-production.yaml. That makes the renamed port safe to keep, so it doesn't need rolling back. Nothing under `src/` reads the port name; the comment in values-production.yaml says so too.

The test: the scrape.yaml comment says "Nothing checks that the two agree", so I added `tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py` as that check. It reads `portName` from the `metrics:` block of values-production.yaml and every `port:` entry under the ServiceMonitor's `endpoints:`, then asserts they match. It uses plain line reading, because I found no YAML library imported anywhere in the repository. Against main as it stands, it should fail, comparing `metrics` with `http-metrics`. With this change it should pass, and it should catch the next rename that only updates one of the two files. Nothing has run it yet.

# How the platform's Prometheus collects the shop's metrics.
#
# The ServiceMonitor the platform applies with the shop's chart, kept in the
# repository beside how the shop is deployed, so that how it is collected
# changes in the same pull request as what it is collected from.
#
# It selects the shop's Service by label, then the endpoint to scrape on that
# Service by the port's *name* - never its number - so a port can move without
# anything here being touched.
#
# The name here has to be the one `metrics.portName` in values-production.yaml
# gives the port. A name that matches no port is not an error to the operator,
# it is a target list with nothing in it - so
# tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py checks that the two agree.
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: io-shop
  labels:
    release: prometheus
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: io-shop
  endpoints:
    - port: http-metrics
      path: /metrics
      interval: 15s

input.summary: Point the ServiceMonitor at the renamed `http-metrics` port and add a test that the scrape port name matches the deployed one
